name: John Rawls
summary: Rawls defended equal basic liberties, fair opportunity and institutions improving the position of the least advantaged. His mature theory favoured dispersed productive wealth or liberal socialism over welfare capitalism. Internationally, he combined assistance and qualified non-intervention with toleration of decent non-liberal societies.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: §43 prefers income transfers to minimum-wage regulation.

public-ownership.rationale: §42 leaves private ownership versus liberal socialism open.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: §49 supports progressive taxes against excessive wealth concentration.

property-fundamental.rationale: §52 contrasts basic personal property with conditional productive ownership.

regulate-corporations.rationale: §43 requires regulation to preserve fair opportunity.

worker-ownership.rationale: §52 accepts cooperatives; their superiority remains unsettled.

state-harmful.rationale: Wenar describes just state institutions as essential to Rawls’s project.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: §50 admits same-sex families compatible with children’s wellbeing.

abortion-legal.rationale: Note 39 confirms his own support for first-trimester abortion.

more-religion-public.rationale: He welcomes religious political arguments, provided public reasons also support coercive policies.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: §6 endorses abolitionist and civil-rights demands for equal justice.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: His quoted letter values European countries’ separate traditions and historical memories.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: pp. 42–43 propose cooperative trade, banking and UN-like institutions.

free-trade.rationale: pp. 42–43 support trade under fair background rules.

nation-first.rationale: Principle 6 subordinates national-interest calculations to moral war limits.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: pp. 37–38 allow intervention against grave rights violations.

revolution-justified.rationale: §55 allows militant resistance under sufficiently unjust conditions.

tax-inheritance.rationale: §49 supports progressive taxation of inherited receipts.

basic-income.rationale: §53 excludes subsidies for voluntarily nonworking surfers.

one-party-rule.rationale: §1 endorses representative constitutional government and political contestation.

democracy-best.rationale: §7 upholds constitutional democracy despite disagreement over majority decisions.

political-violence-never.rationale: He explicitly defends just defensive warfare.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: §4 requires public reasons beyond sectarian scriptural authority.

equal-outcomes.rationale: §46 rejects equal wealth; §18 requires fair distributive outcomes.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: §46 accepts natural beauty itself as a conservation reason.

limit-population.rationale: pp. 109–110 favour lowering fertility through women’s equality.

means-match-ends.rationale: Principle 5 requires wartime conduct to foreshadow just peace.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: §79 opposes demeaning work, not all specialisation.

taxation-theft.rationale: §43 treats taxation as legitimate institutional provision.

conscription.rationale: §58 permits conscription only to defend liberty.

positive-liberty.rationale: p. 50 requires material means for effective freedom.

total-state.rationale: §1 exempts associational background culture from public-reason requirements.

territorial-expansion.rationale: p. 8 rejects conquest as a territorial remedy.

work-for-welfare.rationale: §53 expects work under fair cooperative conditions.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: §50 excludes gender distinctions restricting equal rights.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: §50 identifies injustice in women’s disproportionate care burdens.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Wenar’s account requires substantial social provision beyond security and property.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Wenar identifies citizens’ equal status as basic to Rawls’s justice principles.

consent-of-governed.rationale: §1 requires justification to free, equal citizens, not actual unanimity.

separated-powers.rationale: §36 endorses checks protecting equal political liberty.

priority-to-poor.rationale: §18 prioritises the least advantaged, subject to liberties.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: His letter criticises US-style European federation; his book accepts looser cooperation.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Wenar emphasises liberty’s priority over economic gains.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: §15 requires assistance until decent self-government becomes possible.

collective-defense.rationale: pp. 41–42 permit collective security and allied defence.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: §38 makes public legality essential to liberty.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: §50 excludes apostasy as a legal crime.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: §44 requires constitutional protection of basic liberties.

minority-veto.rationale: §7 rejects unanimity as necessary for legitimate law.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: §77 grounds humane duties in animals’ pleasure and pain.

paid-care-work.rationale: §50 supports equal marital income shares recognising care.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: His quoted letter condemns profit-driven globalisation’s meaningless consumerism.

job-guarantee.rationale: p. 50 endorses government as employer of last resort.

democratic-peace.rationale: §5 argues well-ordered democratic peoples do not fight each other.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: §53 grounds compliance in duties supporting just institutions.

non-intervention.rationale: pp. 37–38 expressly qualify non-intervention for grave abuses.

suppress-opposition.rationale: §2 requires political voice for new groups and interests.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: He condemns domination and exploitation of subjected peoples.

assisted-dying.rationale: He defended a constitutional right while acknowledging reasonable objections to immediate judicial recognition.

social-market-economy.rationale: Wenar describes competitive markets constrained by fair opportunity and dispersed ownership; welfare capitalism alone is insufficient.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: §38 requires legality and independent, impartial courts.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Wenar explains how concentrated wealth undermines effective equal political liberty.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: §34 requires neutrality toward belief and unbelief.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Principle 3 permits attacking soldiers when defence requires it.

person-over-state.rationale: Wenar explains that basic individual liberties cannot be sacrificed for aggregate economic advantage.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: pp. 8–9 also permit extreme humanitarian interventions.

future-generations.rationale: p. 8 requires preserving territorial environmental integrity in perpetuity.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: §58 supports selective refusal, rejects general pacifism.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: p. 9 retains deterrent weapons while outlaw states threaten.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: §34 prohibits religious affiliation penalties or preferences.

negative-income-tax.rationale: §43 permits a negative income tax as the social minimum.

women-suffrage.rationale: p. 110 advocates women’s equal political participation.

national-church-status.rationale: §34 forbids state favour for particular religions.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: §53 says some unjust laws remain binding.

notes: The revised Theory was downloaded and searched. The Law of Peoples scan was downloaded, OCR processed and searched across themes. Local downloads of Restatement and some shorter works were blocked; available browser texts and authorised excerpts were read. Later Restatement positions control revisions. Public Reason Revisited is an independently published 1997 essay. Decent hierarchical regimes are objects of international toleration, not his domestic ideal. Open institutional questions remain qualified. Genetic-policy speculation does not establish restricting reproduction. Property ownership does not settle women’s inheritance specifically. His stationary-state arguments do not establish a particular climate policy. No historical inferences were used.
